speaker: Doctor
text: At what age did the infant first pass meconium, and has this bilious vomiting been present since the first feeding? I also need to know if there is any family history of chronic constipation or neurologic conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Rectal Suction Biopsy

I am ordering an abdominal X-ray to check for dilated bowel loops and a rectal suction biopsy to test for the absence of ganglion cells, which would confirm Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Rectal Biopsy: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The diagnostic tests confirm the absence of ganglion cells, which is pathognomonic for Hirschsprung disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
